text:
dana_support: customer ticket #ZEN-901 reporting OAuth login failing for Google SSO only. They see "invalid_request: missing_state" after redirect back to our /auth/google/callback. Desktop works, but their Android and iOS app (in-app webview) fail. They pasted the full redirect flow they see.

frank_mobile: quick Q - are they using a custom URI scheme (myapp://) for the redirect, or an https callback? Many mobile apps use a custom scheme and rely on the app to pick up params from the fragment. If we expect state on the server side, that won't work.

dana_support: customer says their app uses mycompany://auth#code=...&state=abc123 (they implemented PKCE and stored code_verifier in native storage). They said the developer who integrated us copied the sample that shows fragment-based redirect.

auth-bot: note: OAuth best-practices: redirect URI fragments are not sent to the server; fragments are client-side only. Using fragment-based redirect with a server-side callback will drop state. See RFC6749 sections on redirect URIs.

dmitri_backend: that explains missing_state. Our /auth/google/callback endpoint expects state in query param (req.query.state). When the redirect is to a custom scheme with a fragment, the browser never sends that fragment to our origin. If the app handles the fragment, it must forward the state back to our server or validate on the client with an out-of-band flow.

eva_idps: also remember Google Identity Services default flow for native apps often recommends using an external browser (ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs) with an https redirect to a loopback or claimed HTTPS scheme, not fragments. Using fragments + webview has security and compatibility pitfalls.

frank_mobile: customer dev posted their integration snippet:```js
// mobile app JS running inside webview
window.location = 'mycompany://auth#code=' + code + '&state=' + state;
// The native side reads location.hash and completes login by calling our backend /mobile/complete with {code, state}
```
They say native side calls our backend with the code but sometimes state is empty.

dmitri_backend: how are they sending the code to our backend? If the native side calls /mobile/complete POST with {code, state}, we validate state against a server-side session cookie created earlier at /auth/start. But webviews often isolate cookies (or the native call doesn't include cookies), so server has no session and state can't be matched -> missing_state. Two problems: fragment vs query, and state persistence across webview/native boundary.

dana_support: customer provided our server logs around the failed attempt: `POST /mobile/complete 400 "missing_state" uid=9876 ua="MyAppWebView/1.2"` They also provided a HAR where the original /auth/start set a session cookie with path=/ and SameSite=Lax.

eva_idps: SameSite=Lax is probably okay for top-level navigations but might be dropped for POSTs initiated by the native layer. We should not rely on browser cookie sessions for mobile app/native handoffs. For native flows, best to use PKCE and include a short-lived state stored server-side keyed to the code_verifier or to the state value and return a one-time token. That way the native client can POST code+state and the server can validate using storage rather than session cookie.

dmitri_backend: agreed. We can offer two immediate mitigations for the customer: 1) Change integration to use an https redirect back to our server with query params (e.g., https://app.mycompany.example/auth/mobile/callback?code=...&state=...), then use a deep link/intent redirect from that page to the app (bridge page that includes JS to call myapp:// with the params in the fragment) — this ensures our server sees state and can validate against session/DB. 2) If they must use custom scheme direct-to-app flow, have the native app include state when calling our backend and have the server lookup state in a short-lived datastore keyed by the original nonce (we can provide a small API).

frank_mobile: customer says they can't change app quickly. Any server-side quick fix?

dmitri_backend: temporary workaround: accept state via a one-time exchange token created at /auth/start. Flow: at /auth/start we generate nonce N, persist N -> expected_state in redis with ttl 5m and return a short URL to the client like https://auth.example/complete?nonce=N. The mobile redirect can call mycompany://auth#nonce=N&code=... and the native app can POST code+nonce to /mobile/complete and we validate using redis instead of relying on cookies. We can implement a small compatibility endpoint for customers in a few hours. But need to be careful: nonce must be single-use and tied to client_id and redirect_uri to avoid CSRF.

auth-bot: security note: never accept state-less code exchanges. Any workaround must validate client and redirect origin. Nonces must be single-use and TTL-limited; log and alert on repeated reuse.

dana_support: customer asked if PKCE alone is enough. They used PKCE but still saw missing_state.

eva_idps: PKCE prevents code interception but does not replace state for CSRF protection. You need both PKCE (to bind code to client) and state (to bind request to initiation). For native apps, use PKCE + server-side short-lived storage keyed to a nonce the native app can pass back.

frank_mobile: I can push a patch to our mobile SDK docs showing recommended flow using our /auth/start -> external browser -> https callback -> bridge page -> deep link. But for this customer I can also give them the temporary nonce flow if they want.

dmitri_backend: I'll sketch the server-side endpoint and put it behind a feature flag: POST /mobile/complete {code, nonce, pkce_verifier} -> server looks up nonce -> expected_client_id/redirect_uri, swap code for token with Google including pkce_verifier, mark nonce used. Will add logging: metric oauth.mobile_nonce_exchanges and audit events for reuse attempts.

auth-bot: proposed config change deployed to staging at 2026-03-15T12:30Z for review.

(1h later)

dana_support: customer tried the new nonce endpoint and reports success on Android and iOS in their in-app flow. They accepted the temporary fix and will coordinate an app update in next sprint to move to the bridge-page approach.

frank_mobile: I'll update mobile SDK docs and send sample code for both flows.

dmitri_backend: followup: we'll add a KB article explaining fragment vs query vs server callbacks, recommended native flows (ASWebAuthenticationSession / custom tabs + claimed HTTPS or loopback), and sample code for the nonce endpoint. Also add telemetry to count how many customers still using direct fragment->app flows so we can prioritize migration.

dana_support: closing ticket ZEN-901. Customer thanked us and left a comment saying "fast response, appreciated the temporary endpoint".

auth-bot: reminder: file a short postmortem if we see recurrence or if a customer misconfig causes sensitive info leakage. Security team will review nonce rollout tomorrow.

frank_mobile: noted. Thanks all!
